rated_messages.input_message: Try to avoid seeing other people smoke. It might sound basic but brain see, brain want! If you can, make life easier and avoid the people you used to smoke with for some time where possible.
Maybe you could use these few minutes to work out whose birthday is next and what message you'll write in their card? Then when it comes you'll have something original and well thought-out to write!
Think about times in the past when you have let urges pass during a stressful moment, and notice what helped make that moment easier.
Craving a cig? Plan a fun activity you can do when you get home as a reward for not smoking.
What can you do right now to break the automatic habit of smoking when you are here? Pause. Close your eyes. And take 10 slow breaths.
Instead of lighting up a cigarette, light a scented candle or burn some incense.

You don't have to act on this feeling by smoking or doing anything about it. Give it some space, breathe, and see if it changes. Let the urge and feeling be there while you focus on doing something you care about.
What inspires you most to quit smoking? Are you willing to let this urge pass without smoking for that reason?
You cant always control when you will see other people smoking. But you can control how you respond to your urge when you do.

Write down why you want to stop smoking to resist a craving. Remember, trying something to beat the urge is always better than doing nothing. Each time you resist a cig, you're one step closer to being tobacco-free.
